parts.latex: Which interval gives the range of the function $y=5+2\cos 3x$?

solutions.latex:
Start from the range of cosine, then build up $y$ one step at a time:
$$\begin{aligned} -1&\le \cos 3x\le 1\\ -2&\le 2\cos 3x\le 2 &&(\text{multiply by } 2)\\ 3&\le 5+2\cos 3x\le 7 &&(\text{add } 5)\end{aligned}$$
So $3\le y\le 7$: the range is $[3,7]$.

parts.latex: For what values of $x$, in the interval $0\le x\le\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, does the line $y=1$ intersect the graph of $y=2\sin 4x$?

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned} 2\sin 4x &= 1 \\ \sin 4x &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\ 4x &= \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6} \\ x &= \dfrac{\pi}{24},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{24} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Let $f(x)=\sin(2x)$.

Find the value of $x$, for $0<x<\pi$, for which $f'(x)=-\sqrt{3}$ AND $f''(x)=2$.

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x) &= \sin 2x \\ f'(x) &= 2\cos 2x \\ f''(x) &= -4\sin 2x \end{aligned}$$
When $f'(x) = -\sqrt{3}$,
$$\begin{aligned} 2\cos 2x &= -\sqrt{3} \\ \cos 2x &= \dfrac{-\sqrt{3}}{2} \qquad 0 < 2x < 2\pi \\ 2x &= \dfrac{5\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{6} \\ x &= \dfrac{5\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{12} \end{aligned}$$
When $f''(x) = 2$,
$$\begin{aligned} -4\sin 2x &= 2 \\ \sin 2x &= \dfrac{-1}{2} \qquad 0 < 2x < 2\pi \\ 2x &= \dfrac{7\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{6} \\ x &= \dfrac{7\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{12} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{7\pi}{12} \text{ for } 0 < x < \pi$$
criteria: Finds the values of $x$, $0 < x < \pi$, for each derivative equation
Attempts to find a value for $x$ that solves $f'(x)$ or $f''(x)$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: The function $f(x)=\sqrt{3}\cos(\alpha-2x)$ is odd. Its graph also increases in the interval of $0<x<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. What is a possible value of $\alpha$?

solutions.latex:
Since $f$ is odd, $f(0) = \sqrt{3}\cos\alpha = 0$, so $\cos\alpha = 0$.

$\therefore$ eliminate B and C.

If $\alpha = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x) &= \sqrt{3}\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2x\right) \\ &= \sqrt{3}\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}+2x\right) \\ &= -\sqrt{3}\sin 2x \end{aligned}$$
which decreases on $0<x<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (sketch).

If $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x) &= \sqrt{3}\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2x\right) \\ &= \sqrt{3}\sin 2x \end{aligned}$$
which increases on $0<x<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (sketch).

$\therefore\ \alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

parts.latex:
Consider the function $f(x)=k\cos\left(6x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+c$, where $c$ and $k$ are constants.

The function has a minimum value of $-1$ and a maximum value of $5$.

Which row of the table shows the correct amplitude, period and phase?

solutions.latex:
The amplitude is half the distance between the maximum and minimum:
$$\text{Amplitude} = \dfrac{5 - (-1)}{2} = 3$$
The period of $\cos 6x$ is
$$\dfrac{2\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$$
For the phase, factor the $6$ out of the angle:
$$6x + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 6\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$$
so the phase is $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$.

parts.latex: Determine the values of $x$ for which the graph of $y=3\cos\left(\dfrac{5x-1}{2}\right)$ crosses the $x$-axis in the interval $0\le x\le\pi$.

solutions.latex:
Solve for $x$ when $y=0$:

$$\begin{aligned}3\cos\left(\dfrac{5x-1}{2}\right)&=0\\ \cos\left(\dfrac{5x-1}{2}\right)&=0\\ \left(\dfrac{5x-1}{2}\right)&=\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dfrac{5\pi}{2},\ldots\\ 5x-1&=\pi,3\pi,5\pi,\ldots\end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ x=\dfrac{\pi+1}{5},\ \dfrac{3\pi+1}{5}$$
criteria: Provides one correct solution, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The equation $\cos px=\dfrac{1}{2}$ has 2 solutions where $0\le x\le 2\pi$ and $p>0$.

Find all possible values of $p$.

solutions.latex:
Solve $\cos x=\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $x\ge 0$ first:
$$x=\dfrac{\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{3},\ \ldots$$
\exfigure{1630_q31_s1}

$y=\cos px$ is a horizontal dilation by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{p}$, so its solutions are these values multiplied by $\dfrac{1}{p}$.

Lowest value of $p$ to get 2 solutions (second solution at $x=2\pi$):

\exfigure{1630_q31_s2}
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\times\dfrac{1}{p} &= 2\pi \\ p &= \dfrac{5\pi}{3\times 2\pi} \\ &= \dfrac{5}{6} \end{aligned}$$
Highest value of $p$ (at this value a third solution appears at $x=2\pi$, so it is excluded):

\exfigure{1630_q31_s3}
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{7\pi}{3}\times\dfrac{1}{p} &= 2\pi \\ p &= \dfrac{7\pi}{3\times 2\pi} \\ &= \dfrac{7}{6} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{5}{6}\le p<\dfrac{7}{6}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following correctly describes the order of the transformations of $y=\sin x$ to $y=3\sin(2x-1)$?

solutions.latex:
Order of transformations from $y=f(x)$ to $y=kf(a(x+b))+c$:

\begin{itemize}
\item Horizontal dilation by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{a}$
\item Translate $b$ units left
\item Dilate vertically by a factor of $k$
\item Translate up $c$ units
\end{itemize}

Write the equation in this form:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=3\sin(2x-1)\\&=3\sin\left(2\left(x-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ The transformations are, in order:

\begin{itemize}
\item Horizontal dilation by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$
\item Horizontal translation right $\dfrac{1}{2}$
\item Vertical dilation by a factor of 3
\end{itemize}

parts.latex:
The function $y = 2\sin x + 1$ is translated up $m$ units and then vertically dilated by a factor of $n$ from the $x$-axis, where $m$ and $n$ are positive numbers.

What is the range of the new curve?

solutions.latex:
Translating up $m$ units:
$$y = 2\sin x + m + 1$$
Dilating vertically by a factor of $n$:
$$y = 2n\sin x + mn + n$$
The amplitude is $2n$ and the centre is $y = mn + n$, so the range is
$$[mn + n - 2n,\ mn + n + 2n] = [mn - n,\ mn + 3n]$$

parts.latex: Solve for $x$ where $0\le x\le 2\pi$, $\quad\operatorname{cosec}\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\sqrt{2}$

solutions.latex:
Since $\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)}&=\sqrt{2}\\ \sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$$
Adjusting the domain:
$$\begin{aligned} 0&\le x\le 2\pi\\ \dfrac{\pi}{3}&\le x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\le\dfrac{7\pi}{3} &&\left(\text{add } \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\end{aligned}$$
Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, with related angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$:
$$\begin{aligned} x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}&=\dfrac{\pi}{4} &&\text{(invalid)}\\ &=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\\ &=\dfrac{9\pi}{4}\\ &=\dfrac{11\pi}{4} &&\text{(invalid)}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \therefore\ x&=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \text{ or } \dfrac{9\pi}{4}-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\\ &=\dfrac{5\pi}{12} \text{ or } \dfrac{23\pi}{12}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the correct angles in the shifted domain, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Solve the equation $\tan^2\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+\left(\sqrt{3}+1\right)\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=-\sqrt{3}$, where $0\leq x\leq\pi$.

Give answers in exact form.

solutions.latex:
Rearranging and factorising as a quadratic in $\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$:

$$\begin{aligned}\tan^2\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+\left(\sqrt{3}+1\right)\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+\sqrt{3}&=0\\\left(\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+\sqrt{3}\right)\left(\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+1\right)&=0\end{aligned}$$

So $\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=-\sqrt{3}$ or $\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=-1$.

Since $0\le x\le\pi$, we need $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\le x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\le\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$.

In this range:

$$x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\quad\text{or}\quad x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$$

$$\therefore\ x=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\ \text{ or }\ x=\dfrac{11\pi}{12}$$

parts.latex: Which is the complete solution set to the equation $\sin^2\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$, for the domain $0\le x\le 2\pi$?

solutions.latex:
Taking square roots gives
$$\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$$
Since $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, there are solutions in all four quadrants:
$$x+\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{9\pi}{4},\ \ldots$$
Subtracting $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$:
$$x=\dfrac{\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{13\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{19\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{25\pi}{12},\ \ldots$$
For $0\le x\le 2\pi$ the solutions are $\dfrac{\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{13\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{19\pi}{12}$.

Hence the correct option is C.

parts.latex: What is the change in amplitude and period when the function $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 4x$ is transformed into $g(x)=\sin 2x$?

For $y=a\sin bx$ the amplitude is $|a|$ and the period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{b}$.

The amplitude goes from $\dfrac{1}{2}$ to $1$, so it is doubled.

The period goes from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\pi$, so it is doubled.

Hence the answer is option D.
